title: Fix Dark Pdf Theme Not Applying
description: Dark PDFs are visually identical to light ones because the theme option never reaches the L3 keys system. Fix keys_set expansion in semio.cls, align chrome colors with OS dark theme (navbar/window, foreground text, emblem strokes), and verify dark PDFs render correctly.
summary:
Fixed dark PDFs rendering identically to light PDFs.

Root cause: `\keys_set:nn` in `semio.cls` stored unexpanded macro tokens instead of the theme string, so `\l_semio_theme_tl` never compared equal to `dark` and all theme branches took the light path.

Changes:
- `semio.cls`: `\keys_set:nn` → `\keys_set:nx` so `theme=dark` propagates correctly.
- `semio-core.sty`: removed wrong `semio-chrome-shell` alias; added `semio-chrome-foreground` alias.
- `semio-window.sty`: navbar/footer chips use `semio-chrome-window` (OS `chrome.window`); tcolorbox styles set `coltext=semio-chrome-foreground`; fixed expl3 hbox compatibility for Tectonic.
- `semio-logo.sty`: emblem strokes use `semio-chrome-border-emphasized`; dark logo variant resolution uses `\filename@parse` + `\exp_args:NV \file_if_exist:nTF`.

Verified: `bun ./📜️script.ts test` builds all 12 PDFs; light/dark report title pages visually differ (cream vs `#001117` background, dark vs light text).
